stances.claim: Leonen is not compulsorily disqualified under Sec. 1, Rule 137 (no pecuniary interest, no qualifying relationship, no prior executor role, no prior inferior-court ruling subject to review) -- both Calida and Bongbong concede this and rely on the second paragraph's voluntary-inhibition standard for 'just and valid reasons.'

The July 17, 2017 'Reflection' attributed to Leonen -- urging outright dismissal of Bongbong's protest -- is not enough to disqualify him: 'Reflections' are 'normal, confidential exchanges in the Court even prior to my incumbency in 1995... mere loud thoughts meant to invite discussions on controversial issues... in no way solid, binding opinions.' Justices can modify or reverse them at any time prior to promulgation, and even reverse themselves on reconsideration.

In CJ Panganiban's over 11 years on the Court, voluntary inhibition 'had always been addressed to the sound discretion of the justice concerned' -- 'I do not remember an instance in which the Court forced anyone of us to inhibit when the matter did not fall under the cited Sec. 1, Rule 137.'

Personal precedent: CJ Davide and CJ Panganiban voluntarily inhibited in Estrada v. Desierto at counsel Saguisag's request -- CJ's stated rationale: 'to hold myself above petitioner's reproach and to deprive him or anyone else of any excuse to cast doubt on the integrity of these proceedings' -- though the result was 13-0 with the two inhibitions.

Republic v. Sereno (May 18, 2018) provides the controlling modern formulation: 'the best person to determine the propriety of sitting in a case rests with the magistrate sought to be disqualified,' and forcing the question to the other justices would 'undermine the independence of each of the members of the High Court'; granting the motion would 'open the floodgates to the worst kind of forum shopping.'
Concluding deflection: 'Should Justice Leonen inhibit? Per the above rulings, he is the best person to answer the question.' -- explicitly putting the answer back where doctrine says it belongs.

notable_anecdotes: Calida's 34-page motion with 19 assistant solicitors general -- preserved as evidence of the scale of resources poured into the inhibition effort, in service of the 'Tribune of the People' self-framing.
Bongbong's 'Omnibus Motion' backed by 'legal eagles Juan Ponce Enrile, Manuel M. Lazaro, and Estelito P. Mendoza' -- a who's-who of Marcos-era and elite counsel rolled out for a 21-page motion.

CJ's own self-disclosure that he inhibited (with CJ Davide) in Estrada v. Desierto at Rene A. V. Saguisag's request, with his stated rationale preserved verbatim -- and the parenthetical aside 'In my case though, I have never reversed my vote' as a quiet voicemark on personal consistency.

Sereno June 19, 2018 resolution quoted: granting inhibition would 'open the floodgates to the worst kind of forum shopping... clearly antithetical to the fair administration of justice' -- and the column's deflection close ('he is the best person to answer the question').

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban examines the separate motions filed by Solicitor General Jose C. Calida (34 pages, with 19 assistant solicitors general, invoking 'Tribune of the People' framing) and former senator Bongbong Marcos (21-page Omnibus Motion signed with lead counsel George Erwin M. Garcia and backed by 'legal eagles' Juan Ponce Enrile, Manuel M. Lazaro, and Estelito P. Mendoza) seeking to inhibit Justice Marvic M. V. F. Leonen from the PET protest. Calida alleges partiality from Leonen's Marcos-burial dissent, his Chavez v. Imelda R. Marcos role, and the unreasonable delay since Oct 29, 2019; Bongbong's motion focuses on delay. CJ rules out compulsory disqualification under Sec. 1, Rule 137 (no pecuniary interest, no qualifying relationship, no prior executor role, no prior inferior-court ruling now under review) -- both movants concede this and invoke the second paragraph's voluntary-inhibition standard for 'just and valid reasons.' The alleged July 17, 2017 Leonen 'Reflection' urging outright dismissal is not enough: 'Reflections' are 'normal, confidential exchanges in the Court even prior to my incumbency in 1995... mere loud thoughts meant to invite discussions on controversial issues' -- 'in no way solid, binding opinions,' and justices can modify or reverse them at any time before promulgation (CJ adds the parenthetical: 'In my case though, I have never reversed my vote'). In CJ's over 11 years on the Court, voluntary inhibition 'had always been addressed to the sound discretion of the justice concerned' -- he does 'not remember an instance in which the Court forced anyone of us to inhibit.' Personal precedent: he and CJ Davide voluntarily inhibited in Estrada v. Desierto (March 2, 2001) at counsel Rene A. V. Saguisag's request 'to hold myself above petitioner's reproach and to deprive him or anyone else of any excuse to cast doubt on the integrity of these proceedings' -- Estrada then lost 13-0 with the two inhibitions. The controlling modern doctrine is Republic v. Sereno (May 18, 2018), which held that 'the best person to determine the propriety of sitting in a case rests with the magistrate sought to be disqualified,' and that the June 19, 2018 resolution added that granting compelled inhibition would 'open the floodgates to the worst kind of forum shopping... clearly antithetical to the fair administration of justice.' CJ closes by doctrinal deflection: 'Should Justice Leonen inhibit? Per the above rulings, he is the best person to answer the question.'
